columns.rationale: Two-letter IATA carrier code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16, making it a natural unique key (samples: 9E, AA, DL, UA, WN).
Full airline name with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 matching row_count 16; one name per carrier code (samples: Delta Air Lines Inc., United Air Lines Inc., Southwest Airlines Co.).
Marked is_airbyte_metadata true; capture-tool record identifier with no business meaning, dropped per pipeline convention.

decisions.rationale: carrier has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16, so each carrier code identifies exactly one row; declared as the primary key and error-severity uniqueness rule.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 16, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is applied.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry only capture-tool state (_airbyte_meta holds only {}), so all three are dropped.

purpose: silver_nyc_airlines is a small reference (lookup) table mapping two-letter IATA carrier codes to full airline names for the NYC flights domain, feeding joins that enrich flight-level facts with human-readable carrier names.
usage: Join on carrier (the declared grain and primary key) to resolve airline names; both columns are non-null and the table holds exactly one row per carrier code, so joins are safe without deduplication. Treat it as a static dimension refreshed with each bronze load.
limitations: The cleanup only drops the three Airbyte capture columns; no values were altered. The table reflects a single extraction snapshot (16 rows, duplicate_row_rate 0.0) and covers only the 16 carriers present in the source, so codes outside this set will not resolve in joins.
